description:
About the Position

The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) advertises a three-year funded PhD position in entrepreneurship, artificial intelligence, and labour-market disruption at DTU Entrepreneurship. The research examines how AI technologies reshape entrepreneurial activity and labour markets: which tasks and business models are disrupted, how new venture creation responds, and what the implications are for innovation policy and workforce transition. The position is a salaried doctoral appointment under the Danish collective agreement, based at DTU's Lyngby campus.

DTU Entrepreneurship is a leading European hub for technology-based entrepreneurship research and teaching, combining economics, management and engineering perspectives. The doctoral candidate will combine quantitative empirical work - registry, survey or platform data - with economic and management theory, and collaborate across the centre's project portfolio. The specific project direction is agreed with the supervisory team from the group's current agenda on AI, innovation and work.

Candidate Profile and Application

Applicants hold a master's degree in economics, management, business, innovation studies or a quantitative field, with strong analytical and data skills. Familiarity with econometrics or machine-learning methods applied to economic questions is an advantage. Applications are submitted through DTU's online recruitment system (job 8416) with CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter; the closing date should be confirmed on the official vacancy page.

Highlights

  • 3-year funded PhD at DTU Entrepreneurship
  • AI, entrepreneurship and labour-market disruption
  • Quantitative empirical research with policy relevance
  • Salaried under the Danish collective agreement
  • Leading European technology-entrepreneurship hub
  • Closing date - confirm on the official DTU page

About Technical University of Denmark (DTU)

The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) is one of Europe's leading technical universities, based north of Copenhagen. It ranks among the world's best for engineering and hosts research across energy, computing, biotechnology, robotics and management engineering, including DTU Entrepreneurship as a dedicated hub for technology-based innovation studies. Doctoral candidates at DTU are salaried researchers under the Danish collective agreement, recruited through the university's online recruitment system, and DTU participates extensively in EU Horizon and Nordic research programmes with strong industry collaboration.

  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official page before the deadline: Closing date - confirm on the official DTU vacancy page. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents - early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
